info.title: Frayme API
info.summary: UI for Agents: give your AI a real interface.
info.description:
Your agent calls one API; Frayme streams back live, interactive UI, validated before it renders and built on open standards (json-render, AG-UI, MCP).

Frayme runs its own model, purpose-built for composing interfaces. Every spec is validated before it renders, and weak generations are automatically retried on a stronger model. The `model` field in responses is an opaque identifier: treat it as a string and do not branch on its value.

**Base URL:** `https://api.frayme.ai` · **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer fr_live_…`.

**Billing:** you are billed only for validated successes. Failed generations, in-band `error` events, and idempotent replays are never billed.

**SDK:** `npm i @frayme/api @frayme/runtime`. `@frayme/api` 0.6.0 wraps this exact contract with typed errors, streaming helpers, and automatic idempotency keys on retries.

tags.name: compose
tags.description: Generate validated, interactive UI specs from natural language.

get.description: Unauthenticated liveness probe for the Frayme API. Returns the service name and the active catalog version. Static by design: it does not exercise the model path.

post.summary: Compose a UI from a prompt
post.description:
Turns a natural-language prompt into a validated [json-render](https://json-render.dev) UI spec. This is the product's core endpoint. Requires an API key with the `compose` scope (the default scope on new keys).

By default (`stream: true`) the response is a Server-Sent Events stream (`text/event-stream`) that forwards spec operations live as they are generated. Set `stream: false` for a buffered JSON envelope carrying the fully compiled spec.

### SSE event sequence

OpenAPI cannot model individual SSE frames, so the stream contract is stated here. Every frame is `event: <name>` + `data: <json>`, and the JSON always repeats the event name in a `type` field. A comment keepalive `: ping` is written every 15 seconds (SSE clients ignore comment lines).

1. `compose.started`: first frame. Data: `{type, generation_id, model}`. `model` is an opaque identifier.
2. `op` × N: one frame per json-render operation: `{type: "op", op, path, value?, from?}`. Ops are **provisional**: they pass incremental checks as they stream, but only `compose.completed` finalizes them.
3. `compose.restarted` × 0-1: the attempt failed validation and the generation is retried on a stronger model (at most one restart per request today; treat every one the same way). Data: `{type, generation_id, model, reason: {code}}` where `model` is the identifier the next attempt uses. On this event the client **MUST discard all previously received ops and any rendered state** and rebuild from the following `op` frames.
4. Exactly one terminal frame:
   - `compose.completed`: the **only** success finalizer. Data: `{type, generation_id, model, operation_count, usage: {input_tokens, output_tokens}, validated: true, interactions, components_used}`. Idempotent replays instead carry `replayed: true` and omit `interactions` / `components_used`.
   - `error`: in-band terminal error: `{type: "error", error: {code, message}}` (the HTTP status is already 200 by then). Never billed.

### Modes

- `create` (default): build a fresh UI from the prompt.
- `edit`: pair with `prior_spec`; the server streams a minimal patch that morphs the prior spec in place.
- `continue_journey`: pair with `action_context`; the next step of a flow, composed in context of what the user just did.

### Billing

Exactly one generation is deducted per validated success, committed **before** `compose.completed` is emitted, so a `compose.completed` frame is never a lie. Failures (any `error` frame or non-2xx response) and idempotent replays are free.

### Idempotency

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (≤ 255 chars) to make retries safe. The key binds to the SHA-256 of the exact raw request body. A replay of a completed request is **free** and returns the original `generation_id` with `replayed: true` (as an instant burst-stream when `stream: true`, or the buffered envelope when `stream: false`). Reusing a key while the original request is still in flight returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE`; reusing it with a different body returns `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Keys are retained for 24 hours. The `@frayme/api` SDK generates idempotency keys for its automatic retries, so retried requests can never double-bill.

### Timeouts

Generations typically complete in seconds, but allow a client-side timeout of up to 300 seconds, the server's own ceiling for a single compose.

Unknown request fields are rejected with `400 BAD_REQUEST` (the schema is strict).

value.prompt: Compare our three plans; mark Pro as recommended; a Choose button on each.

actions.name: choosePlan
actions.description: User chose a plan; `plan` is the chosen plan name.

buffered_with_actions.summary: Non-streaming compose with data and a declared action

value.prompt: Refund approval card for the order below: approving is final, so ask before it fires.

200.description: Success. The content type depends on `stream`: `text/event-stream` when `stream` is `true` (the default), `application/json` when `stream` is `false`. See the operation description for the exact SSE event sequence: streamed errors after the 200 arrive as an in-band `error` event.

schema.description: SSE stream. Frames: compose.started → op ×N → (compose.restarted ×0-1, each requiring the client to discard rendered state) → compose.completed | error. Keepalive comment `: ping` every 15 s. See the operation description for each frame's data shape.

bearerAuth.description: API key in the Authorization header: `Authorization: Bearer fr_live_…`. Keys are scoped; `/v1/compose` requires the `compose` scope, which new keys carry by default.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Optional idempotency key (≤ 255 characters) that makes retries safe. Binds to the SHA-256 of the exact raw request body. Completed requests replay free with the original `generation_id` and `replayed: true`; in-flight reuse returns 409; reuse with a different body returns 422. Retained for 24 hours.

ErrorCode.description: Machine-readable error code. **Branch on `error.code`, not on the HTTP status**: several statuses carry more than one code.

ErrorEnvelope.description:
Every non-2xx response uses this envelope. During an SSE stream, errors after the 200 arrive as an in-band `error` event carrying the same `{code, message}` pair.

Full error taxonomy:

| Status | `error.code` | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `BAD_REQUEST` | Malformed JSON, schema violation, unknown field, a size cap exceeded, or an invalid `prior_spec` |
| 400 | `INVALID_MANIFEST` | A `custom_components` manifest failed validation, or two manifests share a name |
| 400 | `CUSTOM_SLICE_TOO_LARGE` | `custom_components` exceed the 12,000-character combined per-request budget |
| 401 | `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` | Missing, malformed, or revoked API key |
| 402 | `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` | Subscription payment past due: update the payment method to resume |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | The key lacks the required scope |
| 403 | `FEATURE_LIMIT` | Reserved for plan limits; not raised today (inline custom components are a 20-per-request cap on every plan, exceeded is a 400 `BAD_REQUEST`) |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Unknown route or resource |
| 409 | `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE` | Same `Idempotency-Key`, original request still in flight |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Same `Idempotency-Key` with a different request body |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Per-key burst limit exceeded: honor the `Retry-After` header |
| 429 | `QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | Monthly generation quota exhausted (no `Retry-After`): upgrade or wait for the next cycle |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` | Unexpected server error |
| 502 | `COMPOSITION_FAILED` | Output failed validation after automatic retries, never billed |
| 503 | `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` | Model backend temporarily unavailable |
| 503 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | Temporary service outage |

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

Spec.description: A json-render UI spec: `root`, `elements` (each `{type, props?, children?, on?}`), `state`, and optional `actions`. Uses standard json-render keys, see https://json-render.dev. Rendered with `FraymeRenderer` from `@frayme/runtime/react`.

theme.description: THE theme dial: `light` or `dark` (≤ 40 characters). Omit to let the host decide. There is deliberately no `signals.theme`.

framework_hint.description: Layout hint for the generator, e.g. `card-heavy` or `dashboard` (≤ 60 characters).

ComposeSignals.description: The primary steering dial: the vocabulary the model reads directly, so these values genuinely move the output. Send only the ones you are confident about; a partial object (or none at all) is a first-class call, and a wrong signal steers worse than a missing one. Most valuable where the prompt alone is ambiguous: "a table of orders" describes both a compact scanning grid and a rich card list, and `density` is what separates them. Theme is not a signal: use `context.theme`.

data_shape.description: What the content IS, one or more of: avatar, board, bracket, calendar, cards, chart, citations, code, diff, document, feed, filters, form, image, link-preview, list, map, plans, reasoning, table, thread, timeline, tree, video.

density.description: How much per screen. `compact`: terse scanning · `standard` · `rich`: generous detail and supporting copy.

patterns.description: Interaction furniture you want available: accordion, bulk-actions, collapsible, confirm-dialog, dialog, drawer, dropdown-menu, hover-card, multi-step, popover, row-actions, segmented-control, tabs, tooltip.

tone.description: `neutral`: product-default styling · `branded`: lean into the colour and voice the prompt describes.

ComposeAction.description: A declared action: Frayme guarantees the wiring: param keys bind to live UI state, and the host receives the resolved values when the action fires.

params.description: The action's params: a JSON Schema object (`{"type":"object","properties":{…},"required":[…]}`) or a flat `{ paramName: { description, enum? } }` map. Keys bind to live UI state and come back resolved when the action fires. List the mandatory keys in `required` (or `requiredItems`): they are marked on the form and genuinely block the submit until filled.

role.description: Short human label for the control that fires this action, e.g. `approve` or `Save board`. Frayme uses it wherever it places or injects the control, including the carrier button injected when the action is wired only to a non-press component. Without it an injected carrier reads "Done" (or a name-derived label when the host is itself a press, or when two carriers on one screen would both read "Done").

live.description: Default false: only a press fires the action (the carrier rule: a Button, a Confirmation verdict, a Form submit, a DataTable, or a row/bulk action on a table or board; any other gesture stays local under `state._ui.<elementId>.<verb>` and rides in the next press's `state`). true = ambient wiring: the action fires on every move/change with no button press (drags, sliders, board moves).

confirm.description: Gate the control behind a confirmation dialog. `true` for a plain confirm; an object (≤ 800 characters serialized) for detail: `{"tone":"danger","body":"This cannot be undone.","confirmLabel":"Delete","denyLabel":"Keep"}`. Unknown keys are ignored, not rejected.

requiredItems.description: The params that are mandatory, lifted to action level: the same claim as `params.required` for hosts sending the flat param map.

required.description: If true, a control bound to this action is guaranteed present: injected if the generation omitted it.

description.description: What this action means / what the user did, for your own handling.

kind.description: How the server closes this action into `spec.actions`: `recompose` re-generates with the fixed `prompt`; `agent` (default) routes the event back to the host agent; `host` posts a message on `channel`; `false` denies the action (inert).

prompt.description: `recompose` only: the fixed prompt the server recomposes with when the action fires.

ComposeActionContext.description: What the user just did on a Frayme-rendered UI: pair with `mode: "continue_journey"` so the next compose responds in context. Serialized size ≤ 16,000 characters. Hosts on `@frayme/api/tools` never build this by hand: `frayme_action` takes the runtime's event (see `FraymeActionInput`) and the SDK maps it here.

action.description: The bound action name the user fired.

event.description: The canonical event verb that fired (`commit`, `select`, `change`, …).

params.description: Resolved param values (the live UI-state values) at fire time.

state.description: Full live-state snapshot: what the user entered; preserved across the recompose.

element_id.description: The spec id of the control that fired: the button, or the table/board whose row/bulk action was pressed (absent only for programmatic dispatches).

generation_id.description: The `generation_id` of the UI the user acted on (correlation).

FraymeActionInput.description: Input of the `frayme_action` tool (`@frayme/api/tools`): the `DynamicActionEvent` your host receives from `@frayme/runtime` when the user presses a control bound to a declared action, forwarded verbatim, plus an optional steering `prompt` and the next screen's `data`, `actions` and `signals`. This is not a request body. The SDK maps it onto `ComposeRequest`: `prompt` becomes the top-level `prompt` (defaulting to a continue-the-journey instruction), `mode` is set to `continue_journey`, `action`, `event`, `params`, `state`, `element_id` and `generation_id` become `action_context`, and `data`, `actions` and `signals` become the top-level fields of the same name. `label` and `description` are accepted for the host's own use (heading a thread card) and are not sent to the server.

action.description: The bound action name the user fired (from a prior `frayme_compose` actions contract).

event.description: The canonical event verb that fired: `commit`, `select`, `change`, `dismiss`, `search`, `sort`, `page` or `move`.

params.description: Resolved params: the live UI-state values at fire time.

state.description: Full live state snapshot: what the user entered; preserved across the recompose. `state._ui.<elementId>.<verb>` holds the latest gesture per verb, never cleared by a press.

element_id.description: The spec id of the control that fired: the button, or the table/board whose row/bulk action was pressed (absent only for programmatic dispatches).

label.description: The label of the control the user pressed, verbatim (absent for a Form submit, whose `element_id` is the Form), for your own thread card; not sent to the server.

description.description: What the action does, in your own words (from your declared action), for your own thread card; not sent to the server.

generation_id.description: The `generation_id` of the UI the user acted on (correlation).

prompt.description: What to do next; default: continue the journey for this action.

data.description: Facts the next screen must show verbatim, exactly as `data` on `frayme_compose`: the result of what the user just did (the saved record, the new total, the confirmation number) plus anything else the next screen displays. Sent as the top-level `data` of the request, never inside `action_context`.

actions.description: Controls the next screen needs, exactly as `actions` on `frayme_compose`. Re-declare every action the next screen needs, including ones declared on the screen the user just used: an action left out comes back unwired. Sent as the top-level `actions` of the request.

signals.description: Steering for the next screen, exactly as `signals` on `frayme_compose`. Sent as the top-level `signals` of the request.

CustomComponentManifest.description: A BYOC custom-component manifest: the same object you author for `defineFraymeComponent` from `@frayme/catalog` (name, props, events, description). Validated server-side with the identical deep lint the client runs; duplicate names are rejected (`400 INVALID_MANIFEST`). Render the matching React components in your app via `createCustomComponents` from `@frayme/runtime`.

ComposeRequest.description: Request body for `POST /v1/compose`. Field names are snake_case on the wire. The schema is strict: unknown fields are rejected with `400 BAD_REQUEST`.

prompt.description: What to build, in natural language. 1-4000 characters.

stream.description: `true` (default): respond as a live Server-Sent Events stream. `false`: respond with a buffered JSON envelope.

mode.description: `create` (default): fresh UI. `edit`: modify `prior_spec` in place (the server streams a minimal patch). `continue_journey`: next step of a flow (pair with `action_context`).

data.description: Factual content AND exact copy the UI must show verbatim: names, prices, items, counts, headings, disclaimers, button labels. These values render as written and are never invented or altered; anything not in `prompt` or `data` is the model's own invention, so pass `{}` for a UI with no fixed content. Display facts only, no synthetic ids or control flags. Serialized size ≤ 48,000 characters.

actions.description: Declared action contract (≤ 20 entries): Frayme guarantees each `required` action is wired to a control.

action_policy.description: How model-authored actions beyond the declared contract are handled. `open` (default): they stay live; the runtime forwards unmapped actions to the host agent. `declared_only`: the server strips every non-builtin action the contract didn't declare (bindings, `spec.actions` entries, and controls whose only job was a stripped action), so the UI can never grow controls the host didn't ask for.

prior_spec.description: The client's current spec, for `edit` / `continue_journey`. Validated server-side before use. Serialized size ≤ 48,000 characters.

metadata.description: Free-form metadata recorded with the generation's usage log. Serialized size ≤ 24,000 characters.

custom_components.description: BYOC: inline custom-component manifests for this request. Available on every plan, unmetered, capped at 20 per request (`GET /v1/me` → `plan.inlineComponentsLimit`). The combined compiled size is budgeted at 12,000 characters per request (`400 CUSTOM_SLICE_TOO_LARGE`).

ComposeInteraction.description: One wired interaction in the returned UI: the "what can this UI do" summary a host agent reads to know which actions it will receive.

element.description: The element id carrying the binding.

kind.description: The `spec.actions` handler kind, or null when unmapped or denied.

params.description: The binding's params, or null when absent.

generation_id.description: Unique id for this generation (`gen_` prefix). On an idempotent replay this is the ORIGINAL generation's id.

model.description: Opaque identifier of the model build that produced this generation. Values are not stable across releases: do not branch on them.

operation_count.description: Number of json-render operations that built the spec.

validated.description: Always true on success: every returned spec passed full validation before delivery.

replayed.description: Present and true only when this response is an idempotent replay of a previously completed request (never billed).

interactions.description: The wired interactions of the returned UI. Absent on replay.

components_used.description: Sorted unique component types used in the spec. Absent on replay.

catalog_version.description: Version of the active component catalog, e.g. `frayme-0.19.0`.

Me.description: Key introspection payload. Note the camelCase field names: this endpoint differs from compose's snake_case.

tierKey.description: Plan tier key, or null when no tier is configured.

monthlyGenerations.description: Generations included per month on this plan.

rateLimitPerMin.description: Per-key burst limit in requests per minute.

generationsRemaining.description: Generations left in the current cycle.

inlineComponentsLimit.description: Maximum inline custom components (BYOC) allowed per compose request. 20 on every plan: a wire limit, not a plan gate.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request. `error.code` is `BAD_REQUEST` (malformed JSON, schema violation, unknown field, size cap, or invalid `prior_spec`), `INVALID_MANIFEST` (a custom-component manifest failed validation or duplicates a name), or `CUSTOM_SLICE_TOO_LARGE` (custom components exceed the 12,000-character per-request budget).

error.message: Invalid request: prompt, prompt is required

PaymentRequired.description: Subscription payment is past due (`PAYMENT_REQUIRED`). Update the payment method to resume generations.

error.message: Subscription payment is past due: update your payment method to resume generations

Forbidden.description: `FORBIDDEN`: the key lacks the required scope, or `FEATURE_LIMIT`: reserved for plan limits and not raised today (inline custom components are a 20-per-request cap on every plan; more than 20 is a 400 `BAD_REQUEST`).

error.message: API key missing required scope: compose

IdempotencyKeyInUse.description: This `Idempotency-Key` belongs to a request that is still in flight (`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE`). Wait for the original to finish, then retry.

error.message: This Idempotency-Key belongs to a request that is still in flight

IdempotencyBodyMismatch.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was already used with a different request body (`VALIDATION_ERROR`). Use a fresh key for a different request.

RateLimited.description: Two distinct 429s: branch on `error.code`. `RATE_LIMITED`: the per-key burst limit (your plan's requests-per-minute) was exceeded; honor the `Retry-After` header and back off exponentially. `QUOTA_EXCEEDED`: the monthly generation quota is exhausted (no `Retry-After`); upgrade the plan or wait for the next cycle.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Present only for `RATE_LIMITED`.

error.message: Rate limit exceeded: slow down and retry with exponential backoff

CompositionFailed.description: The output failed validation even after automatic retries on a stronger model (`COMPOSITION_FAILED`). Never billed: retry, ideally with a clearer prompt.

error.message: Output failed schema validation after fallback

ServiceUnavailable.description: `MODEL_UNAVAILABLE`: the model backend is temporarily unavailable, or `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`: a temporary service outage. Retry with backoff. Never billed.
